sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Internalization rate measured at 2.5%/min in HeLa cells by 125I-IgG uptake assay; neither ANP, BNP, nor CNP altered internalization rate, consistent with known ligand-independent constitutive internalization of WT NPR-C; surface display fully confirmed.
sites.rationale: NPR3 is a type I single-pass transmembrane receptor with a 26-residue signal peptide (cleaved), a 457-residue extracellular domain (residues 27–483), a single TM helix (484–504), and an intracellular C-terminus (505–541). The paper reports an extracellular FLAG tag on the full-length receptor but names no specific residue; because exactly one extracellular terminus exists (the mature N-terminus after SP cleavage), the junction is unambiguously after residue 26 (G) before residue 27 (G). Python verification confirms residue 26 = G and residue 27 = G, and the tag site is 457 residues from the TM boundary, well clear of any constraint. L2 corroborates the same construct and adds ligand-panel functional data. Full-length FLAG-NPR-C (NPR3) expressed in HeLa and 293 cells; FLAG tag placed in the extracellular domain of the intact, membrane-anchored receptor; surface display confirmed by 125I-IgG binding assay tracking the extracellular FLAG epitope.

sources.claim: To specifically measure internalization of a single receptor, we developed an (125)I-IgG-binding assay that tracks extracellular FLAG-tagged versions of GC-A and NPR-C independently of each other and ligand for the first time. FLAG-GC-A bound ANP identically with wild-type GC-A and was internalized slowly (0.5%/min), whereas FLAG-NPR-C was internalized rapidly (2.5%/min) in HeLa cells. In 293 cells, (125)I-ANP and (125)I-IgG uptake curves were superimposable because these cells only express a single ANP receptor.

literature_notes: L1 and L2 both describe the identical FLAG-NPR-C construct from PMC5180442 and ground a single site. No residue number is stated in either clip, so position is topology_derived from the single extracellular terminus. The C-terminus (residue 541) is intracellular and cannot carry an extracellular tag. No other insertion sites (internal loops, other termini) are mentioned in the ledger for NPR3. Validation is surface_and_function because the 125I-IgG assay directly confirms extracellular FLAG display, and internalization kinetics (the primary function of NPR-C as a clearance receptor) are measured and match WT behavior.
